question:
Patient note:
A 58-year-old woman arrived this morning to the pre-operative intake area in anticipation of an open total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and selective pelvic lymph node dissection for a recently staged, grade 2 endometrioid adenocarcinoma that was discovered on dilation and curettage three weeks ago after several months of abnormal uterine bleeding. She parked in the garage, walked the length of the hallway without assistance, and climbed one flight of stairs to the registration desk, describing her usual baseline as fully independent with twice-weekly water aerobics and daily dog-walking; she denies limitations with household chores, yardwork, or climbing two flights of stairs. Her surgical history includes only an uncomplicated laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed eight years earlier, and she has not been admitted to a hospital or undergone any operative or invasive procedure within the last several months. She specifically reports no recent casting, fractures, blunt trauma, strokes, or spinal injuries, and she has not required prolonged bed rest or mechanical ventilation. Medical history is notable for a pulmonary embolus diagnosed seven years ago after she experienced sudden pleuritic chest discomfort and shortness of breath on the final day of a vacation flight from Asia; computed-tomography angiography at that time demonstrated segmental clot in the right lower lobe pulmonary artery without right-heart strain. She completed a six-month course of warfarin, had no recurrence, and has not used chronic anticoagulation since. During that episode, a hematology consultation obtained a thrombophilia panel that revealed moderately elevated IgG anticardiolipin antibody on two occasions twelve weeks apart; the remainder of the panel was unrevealing. Since then, repeat antibody titers have remained above reference range but she has experienced no additional venous or arterial events, no unexplained pregnancy losses, and no livedo, ulcers, or neurologic symptoms. She has no chronic lung disease, obstructive airway symptoms, or baseline oxygen requirement and discontinued a 10-pack-year smoking habit more than 20 years ago. She denies orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, exertional chest pain, ankle swelling, or prior cardiology evaluations for ventricular dysfunction. Review of systems is negative for fevers, shaking chills, productive cough, dysuria, abdominal pain beyond her gynecologic complaints, or weight loss apart from a deliberate 5-pound reduction since diagnosis through dietary changes. She takes letrozole 2.5 mg daily as part of neoadjuvant hormonal therapy initiated by gynecologic oncology two weeks ago, as well as vitamin D and calcium; she uses no glucocorticoids, erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, or hormonal contraception, and has never received heparin products that resulted in platelet drops. There is no tunnelled catheter, port, or peripherally inserted central line in place. Family members are generally healthy, and she is unaware of clotting problems in close relatives. On examination she is seated upright, conversant, and appears her stated age. Vital signs: blood pressure 124/72 mm Hg, heart rate 72 beats per minute and regular, respiratory rate 14, temperature 36.7 °C, and oxygen saturation 97 % on room air. Body mass index is 26 kg/m². Conjunctivae are pink; oropharynx clear; neck supple without jugular venous distension. Heart sounds are crisp, S1 and S2 normal without murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Lungs are clear to auscultation with good air movement bilaterally. Abdomen is soft and nondistended; a palpable, mobile, nontender uterine fundus extends just above the pubic symphysis; no hepatosplenomegaly or ascites is appreciated. Extremities are warm with palpable radial and dorsalis pedis pulses 2+ bilaterally. Calves are symmetric without pitting, tenderness, erythema, cord-like structures, or superficial varicosities. No edema is present at the ankles, and there is full active range of motion of hips, knees, and ankles without discomfort. Neurologic exam shows intact sensation and 5/5 strength in all major muscle groups, normal gait, and negative Romberg; cranial nerves II–XII are grossly intact. Skin inspection reveals surgical scars in the right upper quadrant from prior cholecystectomy but no bruises or ulcerations elsewhere. Pre-operative laboratories obtained yesterday show hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, hematocrit 38 %, platelet count 243 × 10⁹/L, white blood cells 6.4 × 10⁹/L, sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 4.2 mmol/L, creatinine 0.86 mg/dL, AST 21 U/L, ALT 19 U/L, total bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, PT 12.3 seconds, INR 1.0, and activated partial thromboplastin time 31 seconds. Electrocardiogram demonstrates normal sinus rhythm without ST-segment changes, and a recent chest radiograph is unremarkable. An anesthesia airway assessment graded a Mallampati II with good mouth opening and thyromental distance; no predictors of difficult intubation were identified. She has remained fasting since midnight, has taken her morning antihypertensive but held the aromatase inhibitor as instructed, and currently has a single 20-gauge peripheral intravenous catheter in the dorsum of the left hand for fluids and peri-operative medications. The surgical team anticipates an operative duration of approximately three hours under general endotracheal anesthesia with lower-abdominal midline incision, estimated blood loss under 300 mL, and post-procedure admission to the surgical floor for recovery and early ambulation.

Question: What is the patient's Caprini Score for Venous Thromboembolism?
solution:
Apply the Caprini surgical VTE risk score to her preoperative status and planned operation:
- Age 41–60 years: age 58, +1.
- BMI >25 kg/m²: BMI 26, +1.
- Major open surgery lasting >45 minutes: planned three-hour open hysterectomy with lymph node dissection, +2.
- Current or previous malignancy: endometrioid adenocarcinoma, +2.
- History of DVT or PE: prior confirmed PE, +3, even though anticoagulation is complete.
- Documented thrombophilia: persistently positive anticardiolipin antibody, +3, separate from the prior PE.
No additional points for immobility (fully ambulatory), central access (peripheral IV only), or estrogen contraception/replacement (letrozole is an aromatase inhibitor).
Total = 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 3 = 12.
Final answer: 12
